records.text: The Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
“Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in Naboth’s vineyard, because he has gone down there to take possession of it.

Say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because you did murder and did take possession, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where swine and dogs licked Naboth’s blood, dogs will lick your blood there, and prostitutes will bathe in your blood.’”
Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” He said, “I have found you, because you have been sold in vain to do evil before the Lord, provoking Him.

Thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I am bringing calamities upon you. I will burn out what remains after you and destroy from Ahab every male who urinates against a wall, both confined and abandoned in Israel.
I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocations you have provoked and because you did cause Israel to sin.’”
To Jezebel the Lord spoke, saying, “The dogs will devour her at Jezreel’s outer wall.”
Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; anyone belonging to him who dies in the plain, the birds of the heavens will eat.
Yet Ahab acted in vain, as he was sold to do evil before the Lord, as Jezebel his wife turned him aside.
He acted most abominably by following the abominations, according to all that the Amorites had done, whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.
Because of the word, Ahab was stricken before the Lord: he went about weeping, tore his tunic, tied sackcloth around his body, fasted, and put on sackcloth on the day he struck Naboth the Jezreelite.
The Lord’s word came through His servant Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said,
“Have you seen how Ahab has been stricken before Me? I will not bring the harm in his days, but in his son’s days I will bring the harm.”
Thou didst hate those who guard vanities to no purpose; but I hoped in the Lord.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He brought them out of their distresses,
and commanded the storm, and it settled into a breeze, and its waves fell silent.
They rejoiced because they became quiet, and He guided them to the harbor of their desire.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
let them exalt Him in an assembly of the people and praise Him where the elders sit.
